sA1.text:
TODAY · BIRTHDAY LINE
A separate glass capsule 8 pt under the date chip (its own glass, never merged with the chip). Height 34, padding 15 / 12, SF 13/500 ink, chevron-forward-small 8 × 14 ink3, hit area 44.
Shown only on the day and only for catalogue composers with a known day and month. The same line whether or not today’s piece is by the composer. Paging back to earlier days hides it.
Motion: fades in over 300 ms ease-out, 400 ms after Today settles. Reduce Motion: no delay, no fade.
Reduce Transparency: solid surface with a 1 pt outline, like other glass.
Notifications off: this line and the sheet carry the whole message; nothing else is added.

sA2.text:
BIRTHDAY SHEET
Large detent, solid, radius 38. Portrait: 300 pt cover crop at focal_y, as in the composer sheet. Overline SF 12/600 +0.1em accent; name Literata 30/1.15; born line SF 14 ink2; tribute Literata 17/1.6, two or three lines, from a new composers.yaml field (en/tr); gift line SF 15 accent between hairlines; rows are Library rows.
SIGNATURE (proposal, shown as a placeholder)
The autograph is traced from the public-domain Wikimedia Commons scan into one SVG path per pen stroke. 56 pt high, ink colour, left aligned under the tribute. It is drawn on stroke by stroke (strokeEnd 0 → 1), about 1.6 s in total, ease-in-out, starting 250 ms after the sheet settles, once per day. Reduce Motion: shown complete, no drawing. No autograph on file: the block is left out.

sA3.text:
CALENDAR RULES (real catalogue cases)
• Add an explicit birthday (MM-DD) per composer; never parse the facts text.
• Russian composers use Gregorian dates, as printed: Tchaikovsky 7 May (Julian 25 April), Rachmaninoff 1 April, Mussorgsky 21 March.
• Bach (21 March) and Handel (23 February) are printed Old Style; keep these traditional days.
• Beethoven: only the baptism is known, 17 December 1770. The line reads “Beethoven’s day · 257 years” and the sheet says “Baptised 17 December 1770, Bonn”.
• Rossini, 29 February: marked on 28 February outside leap years.
• Allegri, Tallis, Palestrina (year only) and Pachelbel (baptism only): no birthday.
• Shared day: Brahms and Tchaikovsky, 7 May. One line, one sheet, both gifts.
• Age = current year − birth year. Mozart on 27 January 2027: 271.

sA4.text:
THE GIFT (decided)
On the birthday, every piece by that composer is open to free users for the local calendar day.
isLocked = !premium && !isToday && composer.birthday != today.
Library row: the lock becomes the usual chevron and the meta line gains “· Open today” in accent (SF 13). No badge; other rows are unchanged. One on-paper line under the filters, that day only; tapping it filters to the composer.
A piece opened before midnight stays readable until its page is closed.
THE NEXT DAY (recommended: one gentle touch)
Only for a user who opened a gift piece: one on-paper line in Library for that one day, dismissible. Never on Today and never a paywall by itself. Alternative: nothing at all.

sA5.text:
MEDIUM WIDGET
Same layout as now (painting 146 pt, text on the right). Only the overline changes: “TODAY · WED 27 JAN” becomes “MOZART’S BIRTHDAY · 271” in accent (widgetAccentable). Short name, minimumScaleFactor 0.8; if it still does not fit, “BORN ON THIS DAY”. The painting stays free of text. A tap opens Today, which shows the birthday line.

sA6.text:
BIRTHDAY REMINDER
Local notification at the user’s reminder time, one per day scheduled ahead. Attachment: the bundled portrait, pre-cropped to a face-centred square of 600 × 600 px. The crop window is centred at focal_y of the portrait height (Mozart 0.3, Tchaikovsky 0.18) and clamped to the image. Pre-cropping means iOS does not choose the thumbnail crop.
Title: “{short name}, {age} years”. Body: born line, today’s piece, then the gift line for free users only. Re-schedule when Premium status changes. If the day’s piece is not known when scheduling, drop the piece sentence.
Notifications off: nothing else is sent. The Today line carries the message alone.

sA7.text:
SHARED DAY COPY (7 May)
EN title: Brahms and Tchaikovsky
EN body: Both born on 7 May: Brahms in 1833, Tchaikovsky in 1840. All their pieces are open today.
TR title: Brahms ve Çaykovski
TR body: İkisi de 7 Mayıs doğumlu: Brahms 1833, Çaykovski 1840. Bugün bütün eserleri açık.
Premium: drop the last sentence. Attachment: the composer of today’s piece, otherwise the elder.

sB1.text:
CODA BLOCK
A new block between Threads and Recommended recordings. Hairline on top with 44 above and 28 below, the Threads rhythm. Section label “Coda”. Card preview 132 × 165 (the 4:5 card scaled down, radius 6, 0.5 pt ring, soft shadow); line in Literata italic 19/1.45; solid umber 52 pt button with the share icon at 20 pt and “Share this piece”. All solid: it is reading content, not glass. Preview and button both open the share preview sheet.
SHARE THIS MOMENT
Long-press (0.4 s) on a stop card: the card lifts (scale 1.02, deeper shadow), haptic, and a system context menu shows one item, share icon + “Share this moment”. VoiceOver: a custom action on the card. Reduce Motion: no lift.

sB2.text:
SHARE FLOW
1. Preview sheet, medium detent: card preview, segmented Story 9:16 | Post 4:5 (Post by default), solid “Share”.
2. System share sheet with the image and the text + link. Image rendered on device at 1080 px wide, sRGB, JPEG 0.9.
Link: dailyclassical.co/app?utm_source=app-share&utm_medium=piece&utm_content=<piece-id>. Moments use utm_medium=moment.
LINK PREVIEW
Serve link-preview bots an HTML page with Open Graph tags instead of the redirect; people still go to the App Store. og:image 1200 × 630, the painting alone, cover crop at its focal point, no text. og:title = composer short name + title. og:description = the hook + “A listening guide on DailyClassical.”

sC1.text:
DIRECTION 1 · WALL LABEL (recommended)
The painting hangs whole on paper, like a plate on a museum wall, with the label underneath. It is never cropped, so landscape and portrait paintings need no special handling: story = aspect-fit in 912 × 680; feed landscape = 936 wide; feed portrait = 470 wide beside the label.
Type, in px at 1080: composer SF 32/500 accent · title Literata 66/1.12 (feed 54) · hook Literata italic 38 · stop time SF 26/600 accent · stop line Literata 40/1.32 · credit SF 22 · wordmark Literata 36/500 · URL SF 26.
Story: 250 px at top and bottom carry no text.
Moment: the same plate, smaller; the stop line is the headline (Literata 64/1.18).
One fixed paper look in both themes. The dark variant at the end of the row is for comparison.

sC2.text:
DIRECTION 2 · PAINTING-LED
The painting fills the top edge to edge and the text sits on paper below. The strongest thumbnail, and the closest to the Today screen.
Cost: the painting is cropped (cover at its focal point). A landscape painting loses its sides in story size; a portrait painting loses top and bottom in feed size.

sC3.text:
DIRECTION 3 · PROGRAMME NOTE
Type-led and centred, like a concert programme: title first, movements listed, the painting as a small plate. The most readable at small sizes.
Cost: the painting, which gives the app its colour, becomes secondary, and the card is quieter in a feed.
